title: Verbum supernum, st. 1
source: Verbum supernum prodiens, nec Patris linquens dexteram (St Thomas Aquinas)
text: Verbum supernum prodiens, Nec Patris linquens dexteram, Ad opus suum exiens, Venit ad vitæ vesperam.
notes:
English: The Heav'nly Word proceeding forth, / Yet leaving not the Father's side, / And going to His work on earth / Had reached at length life's eventide.

Latin: Verbum supernum prodiens, nec Patris linquens dexteram, St Thomas Aquinas; Britt 1922. English: J. M. Neale (st. 1-4) and Edward Caswall (st. 5-6), as printed in Matthew Britt, The Hymns of the Breviary and Missal (London: Burns Oates & Washbourne; copyright 1922 Benziger Brothers, printed in U.S.A.), p. 188 (archive.org/details/hymnsofbreviarym00britrich). Both public domain.

title: Verbum supernum, st. 2
source: Verbum supernum prodiens, nec Patris linquens dexteram (St Thomas Aquinas)
text: In mortem a discipulo Suis tradendus æmulis, Prius in vitæ ferculo Se tradidit discipulis.
notes:
English: By false disciple to be given / To foemen for His Blood athirst, / Himself, the Living Bread from Heaven, / He gave to His disciples first.

Latin: Verbum supernum prodiens, nec Patris linquens dexteram, St Thomas Aquinas; Britt 1922. English: J. M. title: Verbum supernum, st. 3
source: Verbum supernum prodiens, nec Patris linquens dexteram (St Thomas Aquinas)
text:
Quibus sub bina specie Carnem dedit et sanguinem;
Ut duplicis substantiæ Totum cibaret hominem.
notes:
English: To them He gave, in two-fold kind, / His very Flesh, His very Blood: / In love's own fulness thus designed / Of the whole man to be the food.

Latin: Verbum supernum prodiens, nec Patris linquens dexteram, St Thomas Aquinas; Britt 1922. English: J. M. title: Verbum supernum, st. 4
source: Verbum supernum prodiens, nec Patris linquens dexteram (St Thomas Aquinas)
text:
Se nascens dedit socium, Convescens in edulium, Se moriens in pretium,
Se regnans dat in præmium.
notes:
English: By birth, our fellow-man was He; / Our meat, while sitting at the board; / He died, our ransomer to be; / He ever reigns, our great reward.

Latin: Verbum supernum prodiens, nec Patris linquens dexteram, St Thomas Aquinas; Britt 1922. English: J. M. title: Verbum supernum, st. 5
source: Verbum supernum prodiens, nec Patris linquens dexteram (St Thomas Aquinas)
text:
O salutaris hostia,
Quæ cœli pandis ostium,
Bella premunt hostilia,
Da robur, fer auxilium.
notes:
English: O saving Victim, opening wide / The gate of heaven to man below, / Our foes press on from every side, / Thine aid supply, Thy strength bestow.

title: Verbum supernum, st. 6
source: Verbum supernum prodiens, nec Patris linquens dexteram (St Thomas Aquinas)
text:
Uni trinoque Domino, Sit sempiterna gloria:
Qui vitam sine termino Nobis donet in patria.
notes:
English: To Thy great Name be endless praise, / Immortal Godhead, One in Three; / O grant us endless length of days / In our true native land, with Thee.
